output.question: What lawsuits involve Celsius?
output.answer: As of 2026-11-11, the principal proceedings involving Celsius Network are: (1) its Chapter 11 bankruptcy case, Celsius Network LLC et al., No. 22-10964(MG), in the Southern District of New York; (2) the SEC civil enforcement action, SEC v. Celsius Network Limited and Alexander Mashinsky, No. 1:23-cv-06005, alleging securities-offering, fraud, and market-manipulation violations; (3) the CFTC action, No. 1:23-cv-06008, alleging fraud, material misrepresentations, and unregistered commodity-pool activity; and (4) the FTC action against Celsius entities and executives over alleged deceptive promises about customer deposits. Related proceedings include the criminal case against former CEO Alexander Mashinsky (No. 1:23-cr-00347-JGK), which ended with a guilty plea and a 12-year sentence, and bankruptcy adversary matters such as Celsius Network LLC v. Symbolic Capital Partners Ltd. The bankruptcy docket also lists adversary proceedings and a consolidated customer-preference-actions docket, so this is a summary of the major proceedings rather than a claim that every related adversary action is listed.

key_facts.fact: Celsius Network LLC et al. is in Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the Southern District of New York, case No. 22-10964(MG); the CFTC states Celsius filed for bankruptcy on July 13, 2022.

The SEC filed SEC v. Celsius Network Limited and Alexander Mashinsky, No. 1:23-cv-06005, on July 13, 2023, alleging unregistered offers and sales of securities, false or misleading statements, and manipulation of CEL.

The CFTC filed against Alexander Mashinsky and Celsius Network LLC on July 13, 2023, alleging fraud, material misrepresentations, and unregistered commodity-pool-operator and associated-person activity; Celsius agreed to a permanent injunction, and the action against Mashinsky was resolved by consent order on June 18, 2026.

The FTC case names Celsius Network Inc. and multiple Celsius affiliates plus Alexander Mashinsky, Shlomi Daniel Leon, and Hanoch Goldstein; the FTC says the defendants were charged over deceptive claims that customer deposits were safe and always available, and reports a total $16.5 million resolution for the founders.

The related criminal case is USA v. Alexander Mashinsky, No. 1:23-cr-00347-JGK; according to the CFTC, Mashinsky pleaded guilty on December 3, 2024, and was sentenced on May 8, 2025 to 12 years in prison, a $50,000 fine, and forfeiture of $48,393,446.

A bankruptcy adversary proceeding is Celsius Network LLC v. Symbolic Capital Partners Ltd., No. 24-03997-mg; on June 23, 2025, the Bankruptcy Court denied Symbolic's motion to dismiss for failure to timely serve the summons and complaint.

caveats: Celsius is a group of related entities, and the proceedings name different combinations of Celsius Network LLC, Celsius Network Limited, Celsius Network Inc., Celsius Lending, Celsius KeyFi, Celsius Mining, and other affiliates.

The Stretto docket indicates additional adversary proceedings and a consolidated customer-preference-actions docket; the dynamic listing did not expose a complete proceeding-by-proceeding inventory in the opened page.
The FTC page was last updated July 20, 2026 and labels the matter pending, while the CFTC page reports resolutions for Celsius and Mashinsky; procedural status can differ by defendant and agency.
